answer.origin: Primary source: NVIDIA Corporation Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR), dated and reported August 17, 2026, Items 1.01, 2.03 and 7.01, citing NVIDIA's own press release (Exhibit 99.1) and the Agreements as entered that day.
answer.note: NVIDIA's own 8-K states that on August 17, 2026 it entered multiple residual value guaranties with SB Energy as Lessor, covering leases for about 4.25 GW of IT load at the Portsmouth Site (PORTS Technology Campus, Pike County, Ohio), with an affiliate of OpenAI Group PBC as tenant. The filing says NVIDIA can also provide credit support for about an additional 3.8 GW at its sole discretion. Its initial commitment is capped cumulatively at $105 billion. Payments are conditioned on, among other things, the Lessor meeting ready-for-service conditions under the relevant lease, which the company expects to begin in 2028. A Trigger Event (OpenAI insolvency causing lease default, or OpenAI payment failure) would require NVIDIA to pay generally the shortfall between a guaranteed minimum lease value and recoveries from reletting or sale. OpenAI agreed to reimburse and indemnify NVIDIA for amounts NVIDIA actually pays. The Agreements also terminate on the earliest of the 20th anniversary of lease commencement, lease termination by OpenAI, OpenAI reaching a satisfactory credit rating, or other customary events. Reading this as a source claim: the material fact is a binding, contingent credit-support obligation undertaken by NVIDIA, with a stated $105 billion cumulative cap on the initial commitment. The obligation's cash effect depends on a future Trigger Event and on lease commencement, which the company expects in 2028, so it is not a current purchase, revenue or order record. It does show NVIDIA taking on large off-balance-sheet-style credit exposure to back a customer's AI data center capacity, and it links NVIDIA's DSX AI factory platform to OpenAI as the deploying tenant. Conditional interpretation: if the Agreements operate as described, NVIDIA's economic exposure is concentrated in OpenAI's credit and in the timing of ready-for-service at Portsmouth. The 8-K gives no accounting treatment, expected charge, or probability of a Trigger Event.
limitations: The full text of the Agreements is not in the record; the 8-K says the form will be filed as an exhibit to the 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2026, so the guaranteed minimum values, cap mechanics and termination terms are known only as summarized.
No accounting treatment is disclosed for the guaranties, so the recognized liability, fair value, or expected loss is unknown.
The $105 billion cap applies only to the initial commitment; no cap or amount is disclosed for the additional roughly 3.8 GW of optional credit support.
The 8-K does not state lease commencement dates or the per-GW economics; the 2028 ready-for-service timing is a company expectation, not a confirmed schedule.

OpenAI's credit standing and lease terms are not disclosed beyond the stated tenant role and the credit-rating termination trigger, so the likelihood of a Trigger Event cannot be assessed from this source.
The company's statement that it has secured land, power and shell capacity is its own characterization; no independent confirmation is in the record.
The press release (Exhibit 99.1) is referenced but its text is not supplied in the record.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2026 for the filed Agreement form, cap mechanics, guaranteed minimum values, and accounting treatment of the guaranties.
Review Exhibit 99.1 to the August 17, 2026 8-K for any additional figures on timing, capacity, or economics beyond the 8-K text.
In NVIDIA's next periodic filings, check for disclosure of lease commencement, ready-for-service status, any Trigger Event, and whether the optional 3.8 GW credit support has been exercised.
Check SB Energy and OpenAI public disclosures for the Portsmouth lease terms, financing, and any tenant credit developments that bear on the Trigger Event risk.
